headline: Karissa had a night-time bathroom fall on 9/23 and was seen in the ED on 11/5 for dehydration and dizziness. Evening confusion was reported on 11/15, and the PCP documented it as resolved on 11/16.

items.statement: Fall at home on 2026-09-23 in the bathroom at night; her son Marcus found her on the floor. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness, no injury was noted, and fall risk was reassessed as high. PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-09-23 nursing note, including the PT referral.

items.statement: ED visit on 2026-11-05 for dehydration and dizziness; treated and released the same day with no new medications. At the PCP follow-up on 2026-11-11 she was back to baseline per her son, discharge medications were reviewed, and the plan was close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED summary and PCP follow-up note support every detail: same-day release, no new medications, back to baseline per son, discharge medications reviewed, and close monitoring for two weeks.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-01 found gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly. The notes do not show whether the walker, home evaluation or grab bars are in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation note contains all stated findings and recommendations. The caveat that the notes don't show whether the equipment is in place is accurate, since the cited note doesn't say.

items.statement: On 2026-11-15 Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. She was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit. The PCP documented the confusion as resolved on 2026-11-16 and removed it from the problem list. The notes do not show the urinalysis or medication review results.
items.verifier_note: The 11-15 nursing note supports the report, exam findings and plan. The 11-16 PCP note documents the confusion as resolved and removed from the problem list. Neither note gives urinalysis or medication review results, so that caveat is accurate.

questions_for_team: Is the fall on 9/23 related to the dizziness and dehydration seen on 11/5? What is the current fall-prevention plan for night-time bathroom trips?
Have the walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars recommended by PT on 10/1 been completed?
Were the urinalysis and medication review planned on 11/15 completed, and what did they show?
Does the team want to continue monitoring evening confusion and stove safety at home, given the PCP documented it as resolved on 11/16?
What hydration monitoring and support is in place at home and at the day center after the 11/5 ED visit?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, and hospital admissions in that window, plus any discharge summaries not yet reconciled into the chart.
Falls and near-falls: check incident reports and nursing notes for the window, including injury, fall-risk screen results, and any new fall-risk medications.

Medication reconciliation: review the new simvastatin 10 mg start dated 2026-08-16 alongside the existing simvastatin 20 mg entry from 2020-07-11. Check for a duplicate statin or a dose change, confirm which is intended, and confirm the prescriber and reason. Also verify that no other statin or lipid-related order was started or stopped.

Cardiac medications: confirm adherence and refill history for metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, and nitroglycerin spray. Note any missed doses, held doses, bleeding or bruising reports, dizziness, or heart rate and blood pressure changes. Check nitroglycerin use frequency and any chest pain episodes documented in the window.
Vitals trend: review blood pressure and resting heart rate for the window, including orthostatic readings if taken, and flag values outside the team's agreed parameters for the participant.

Weight and BMI trend: compare recorded weights in the window against prior baseline, since the participant has obesity (BMI 30+) and prediabetes. Flag gain or loss of 5% or more, or a sustained trend.

Glycemic monitoring: check any glucose or HbA1c results, point-of-care readings, and diabetes-prevention or dietary counseling notes, since prediabetes is listed. Confirm whether any glucose-lowering therapy was started, which would not appear on the current list.
Lipid and cardiac labs: check whether a lipid panel was drawn or resulted after the simvastatin change, and whether any follow-up lab is due for statin or antiplatelet monitoring.

Breast cancer history (diagnosed 1997): check for any surveillance imaging, oncology follow-up, or survivorship care items that are overdue or due in the window. Note that the chart lists no active oncology medication.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: review ADL and IADL changes, cognitive screen results, mood screen or depression notes, social engagement and program attendance, and caregiver status or strain. Also check that care-plan items due in the window (assessments, consents, reviews) are completed, and list any overdue items.
